items.title: PNV backs first housing decree before November 12 vote
items.body: Two housing decrees approved by the cabinet face a vote on November 12. The PNV, whose votes are decisive, will back the first, which covers seasonal rentals and protects vulnerable tenants and small landlords. It will reject the second, which includes 12 months' compensation from landlords to tenants.

items.title: Housing general strike called for November 11
items.body: Major unions, including CCOO and UGT, back a general strike on Wednesday, November 11, over the housing crisis. The Sindicato de Inquilinas tenants' union drove it after the eviction of Maricarmen. It would be the first major general strike in 14 years. Assemblies are explaining the right to strike.

items.title: Regional tax cuts could reach €2.3 billion
items.body: Approved, draft and announced regional tax cuts could total €2.3 billion through 2031, fiscal watchdog Airef estimates. About 80% of the lost revenue would come from IRPF (personal income tax). Andalusia's draft 2027 budget alone has cuts above €280 million. Airef advises against permanent cuts without enough funding.

items.title: Hazardous-job early retirement requests remain unresolved
items.body: Social Security has not resolved any of the hazardous-job early retirement requests, which cover about two million workers. A Royal Decree approved in May 2025 sets out the process. Transport requests are past the six-month deadline, and unions threaten strikes in road transport.

items.title: Two former central bankers vie for ECB presidency
items.body: Former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos and former Dutch central bank head Klaas Knot are the only candidates to succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB president, the Eurogroup confirmed on November 6. The deadline for nominations has closed.

items.title: EU prosecutors investigate rail funds after Urda crash
items.body: The European Public Prosecutor's Office has opened an investigation into alleged fraud of EU funds meant for renewal and safety work on the Madrid-Sevilla high-speed line. A fatal accident occurred near Urda, Toledo, on that line. Prosecutors have ordered searches at the headquarters of rail manager Adif.

items.title: 442 affordable rentals available from November 7
items.body: State housing company CASA 47 has added 442 affordable rentals across six regions, available from November 7. Applications are open until November 26. Household income must be between 2 and 7.5 times the IPREM income benchmark, and at least one member must have Spanish nationality or legal residence.

items.title: Proposed wage rise would widen subsidy eligibility
items.body: The Economy Ministry proposes raising the SMI (minimum wage) by 5.3% to €1,286 gross a month in 14 payments for 2027. If approved, the monthly income ceiling for most unemployment subsidies would rise from €915.75 to about €964.50. Applicants would still need to meet other eligibility rules.

items.title: Report puts Ceuta border entries above 100,000
items.body: El Mundo calculates that more than 100,000 people entered Ceuta on July 30–31, well above government figures. It uses a Guardia Civil report. The Guardia Civil recorded 88,146 returns to Morocco by October 27. Police estimate 8,000 adults remain, and 3,688 minors are in the city's care.

items.title: Menopause treatment shortages prompt hospital medicine imports
items.body: Spain's medicines agency Aemps now allows hospital imports of hormone treatments because of shortages. Patients pay no extra for imports, but some buying substitutes face higher costs: funded Lenzetto costs about €0.85 at the maximum patient contribution, while unfunded Oestraclin costs about €17.38.

items.title: Judge rejects Zapatero jewel embezzlement investigation
items.body: A judge has refused prosecutors' request to investigate former prime minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero for alleged embezzlement over jewels received in 2007. He ruled that receiving them through public office did not itself make them public property. Tax crime and smuggling charges against Zapatero are separate.
